9.0.0.en: After the Gergesenes rejected Christ, He boarded the boat and returned to His city, that is, Capernaum, which He had taken as a place in which to perform His miracles and give His teachings. By returning to His city He shows us the importance of caring for our homeland, while our hearts are opened wide in love to everyone.

9.0.1.en: It appears here that Christ crossed from the west of the Sea of Tiberias to its east in order to heal the possessed men, and then returned immediately afterward to Capernaum. This shows how precious a single soul is to Christ, how He travels for hours to meet it and save it.

9.1.0.en: This man was struck with paralysis and the attempts to cure him failed. When his four friends heard that Christ had come to Capernaum, they hurried to carry him to Him that He might heal him. The two Evangelists, Mark (Mk 2:3-12) and Luke (Lk 5:18-26), tell us that they found a crowd around the house, so they went up on the roof, broke through it, and let the paralytic down on his bed before Christ, who was sitting among the crowds. When Christ saw the faith of these friends, and saw the cause of this man's illness, which was sin, He granted him forgiveness by the authority of His divinity, which is the greater grace, that is, the healing of the spirit before the healing of the body.

9.2.0.en: Seated around Christ was a group of scribes, who were those who knew the Law, and religious leaders of the Jews. Instead of doing their work as servants of this people, and presenting them to Christ that He might heal them and forgive their sins, they thought evil in their hearts, saying: How does this man speak blasphemies? For, being a man, he speaks as God who has authority to forgive.

9.2.1.en: "Blasphemeth": he claims for himself an authority that belongs to God alone.

9.3.0.en: Jesus knew their thoughts without hearing them, and this confirms His divinity, because none knows the inner thought except God. He rebuked them for their evil thoughts, and this makes clear that an evil thought is sin, and not only the deed and the word.

9.4.0.en: Christ asked the scribes which is easier: the forgiveness of sin or the healing of the body? They did not answer, because they feared Him, since He knew their thoughts without their having spoken them... The answer, of course, is that the easier is the healing of the body. So God, who has authority, gave what is more important, namely forgiveness. Then, as a proof of His divinity, He gave bodily healing, and said to the paralytic: "Arise, take up thy bed (thy couch), and go unto thine house."

9.4.1.en: Taking up the bed: this proclaims the strength of the paralytic's health. The bed reminds a person of the pains of illness, so when he carries it he feels the power of the miracle, remembers his former weakness, and thanks God.

9.4.2.en: The house: it is his former life, and signifies his return to the Church and his relationship with God after being healed of the spiritual illness.

9.4.3.en: "The Son of man": what is meant by it is Christ incarnate.

9.4.4.en: "Power on earth": that is, the authority of God who is in heaven, in forgiving sins and healing the sick, and the ability to do anything.

9.5.0.en: When the crowds saw the greatness of the miracle, they marveled greatly and glorified God, because He had given such great authority to one of men, namely Jesus, since they were not yet able to believe in the Incarnation and divinity of Christ. Praise every good work you see, and do not doubt everything and think evil. The more humble you are, the more you are able to see the virtues of others, and you will judge no one, and will always glorify God.

9.6.0.en: Matthew, the writer of this Gospel, worked as a tax collector, and this profession was associated with cruelty, injustice and the love of money. For the tax collector first paid the Roman authority the tax required for the village or place entrusted to him, and then collected it with the help of the Roman soldiers, so he collected more than he had paid, however poor the people were.

9.6.1.en: But when he saw Jesus and heard His word, his feelings were moved, so he obeyed His call, and left all his work, his money and his sins, relying on Him, and he did not consult his relatives and loved ones lest he be hindered.

9.6.2.en: Here the love and humility of Christ appear, in calling His disciples from among fishermen, or from among the wicked such as Matthew the tax collector, known for cruelty and violence, in order to purify them and fill them with His Holy Spirit, so that the glory is to Him and not to human strength.

9.6.3.en: "The receipt of custom": most likely a large tent, set up on the road for collecting money in it under the guard of Roman soldiers.

9.6.4.en: "Follow me": he may have heard of Christ before and seen Him, so he was ready to obey Him at once when He called him.

9.7.0.en: The tax collectors and sinners: because of the greed and cruelty of the tax collectors, their name became linked with sinners, and they were rejected by Jewish society.

9.7.1.en: After Matthew followed Christ, his heart rejoiced greatly, so he longed that his fellow tax collectors and sinners might enjoy the knowledge of Christ. So with spiritual wisdom he made a feast for Christ, to which he invited all his friends that they might hear and repent of their sins. And Christ accepted the invitation, because He came for the salvation of sinners and not the righteous.

9.8.0.en: But the Pharisees, who held to the outward appearances of the spiritual life and not its essence, and who criticize others with pride, reproached the disciples of Christ because their Teacher sits and eats with sinners. They paid attention to the appearance without seeking the reason for His presence at the feast, that is, His concern for the salvation of these souls.

9.9.0.en: "When Jesus heard": the Pharisees' words were addressed to His disciples, because they were afraid to speak to Him. But He, with power, declared to them their error in keeping away from calling sinners to repentance under the pretext of not being defiled by mixing with them, and Christ showed them the reason for His Incarnation, which is the calling of sinners to repentance. And this is logical, for the physician goes to the sick and not to the healthy; so it is natural for Christ to care for those who are far off, that they may repent of their sins.

9.10.0.en: Jesus rebuked them gently, requiring of their hearts mercy toward sinners, which is more important than offering sacrifices without understanding, because the sacrifice is a symbol of Christ's sacrificing His life on the Cross so that He might have mercy on sinners, and these words were declared before by Hosea (Hos 6:6). ("The righteous": in their own eyes, because there is no righteous man, but all are sinners in need of the redemption of Christ. "Sinners": that is, those well known for their sins, such as the tax collectors.)

9.10.1.en: Care for those who are far off so that you may call them to Christ, and pray for them, and look for ways to draw them to God, if not by direct speech, then by indirect speech, such as speaking with others in their presence, or offering encouraging words or works of love that soften their hearts, until they turn back from their rejection of God.

9.11.0.en: "The disciples of John": some of them followed Christ and became His disciples, and some did not join Him, holding only to John's teachings of repentance and asceticism; so these speakers are not disciples of Christ. "Oft": the Pharisees imposed fasts other than those the Law prescribes, and the disciples of Christ, like most of the Jews, did not keep them.

9.11.1.en: The disciples of John and the Pharisees complained against Christ because His disciples do not fast. This means that they felt the burden of fasting, as an ordinance difficult for them, from which they wanted to be freed, or whose hardship they wanted others to bear along with them; that is, they had the outward form of fasting but did not feel its spiritual blessings.

9.12.0.en: "The children of the bridechamber": the close relatives and friends of the bridegroom.

9.12.1.en: "Mourn": because fasting is linked with humbling oneself, tears and repentance.

9.12.2.en: Christ answered that His disciples, who are the children of the bridechamber while He is their Bridegroom, ought not to fast until after the Bridegroom is taken away; therefore they will fast when Christ ascends to heaven. But during His life on earth they rejoice in Him, and fasting is postponed because it is a sign of humbling oneself and of spiritual striving; and the Apostles did in fact fast after the Ascension of Christ.

9.13.0.en: Christ addressed the real problem, which is the understanding of fasting: it is not a compulsory ordinance, but a love offered to God. If the whole of life is not changed by repentance, we do not benefit from any spiritual practice, because it will be superficial, and will even harm a person since he becomes proud through it.

9.13.1.en: Christ likened this harm to putting a piece of new cloth on an old garment, so that its fabric, being stronger than the old fabric, tears it because of its weakness; thus the new patch does not benefit the old garment, but harms it and tears it.

9.13.2.en: "Old garment": that is, an ancient garment, a symbol of the life of the Pharisees who refused to believe in Christ and who loved pride and various evils.

9.13.3.en: The new patch: it signifies fasting which, if it is not placed in a life renewed by Christian faith, will harm, that is, it will add pride to the Pharisees.

9.13.4.en: And this is a second reason for the disciples' not fasting, since what matters first for them, and for all people, is to believe in Christ and repent of their sins; only then are their worship and fasts accepted.

9.14.0.en: "Bottles": vessels of skin, that is, (waterskins), in which wine or water or any liquid is put. Also, new wine is strong and the old bottles cannot bear it, because the products of fermentation are stronger than the thin skin of the old bottles, so they burst and the wine is spilled. Therefore new wine needs new bottles, whose skin is thick.

9.14.1.en: "Old bottles": that is, old vessels, a symbol of the life of the Pharisees and of John's disciples who did not yet believe in Christ.

9.14.2.en: "New wine": it signifies fasting, which is a spiritual worship that rejoices the heart of God.

9.14.3.en: "New bottles": this is the life renewed in Christ by faith, which bears and is adorned with all spiritual practices such as fasting.

9.14.4.en: May your fasting be joined with repentance and partaking of the Holy Sacraments, and reading the Holy Bible and meditating on it, so that it becomes a spiritual fast that stirs your feelings with love and mercy toward the needy, and you rejoice and long for fasting, because it is a strong means that brings you near to God and delivers your soul from many lusts.

9.15.s.en: (4) The healing of the woman with the issue of blood and the raising of the daughter of Jairus

9.15.0.en: A ruler of one of the synagogues of the Jews came to Christ. These were places spread throughout Judea in which prayers and the reading of the Holy Scriptures were held, while sacrifices were offered only inside the Temple in Jerusalem.

9.15.1.en: This ruler, whose name was Jairus (Mk 5:22; Lk 8:41), came with faith and humility, worshipping Christ, asking Him to raise his daughter, who had died, by coming and touching her, and he believed that she would rise. This is great faith, but the faith of the Gentile centurion is greater, for he said to Christ: "Speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed" (ch. 8:10); he did not need Christ to come to him, but it was enough that He command, and the illness withdraws.

9.15.2.en: The age of the girl, the daughter of Jairus, was twelve years (Lk 8:42), and she points spiritually to the nation of the Jews, which had twelve tribes. She died on her bed, and so she signifies the sin of the inner thought, and Christ is able to raise from this sin.

9.15.3.en: So Christ responded with great love as was His custom, and went to the house of Jairus, and His disciples followed Him to see His miracles and hear His teachings.

9.16.0.en: The woman with the issue of blood had for twelve years been trying to be cured without avail, so she points to the spiritually sick soul, which tried by human means to cure sin and did not succeed.

9.16.1.en: "Behind him": she did not appear before Him, either from shame at her illness, or because the Jews regarded a woman's issue of blood as uncleanness (Lev 15:25-26), and therefore they would not allow her to touch Christ.

9.16.2.en: This woman resorted to Christ to meet Him on the way, like the soul that meets Christ on the road of life through the events of the world, and believes in Him and is healed of its troubles.

9.16.3.en: She believed that merely touching the hem of His garment would heal her, and she did this and was healed. And Christ wanted to glorify the faith of this woman, so He made known what she had done before the crowds, and assured her that she had been healed completely.

9.17.0.en: Christ reached the house of Jairus and found the relatives and loved ones weeping, and even those whom they had hired, the pipe players with their sad tunes, giving forth loud sounds that stir the emotions. So He reassured everyone that the girl was asleep and not dead, although she had in fact died. But by the power of His divinity He is able to raise her; for in His sight the rest of death is like the rest of sleep.

9.17.1.en: But they did not believe and mocked His words, since they could not believe in His power to raise from the dead.

9.18.0.en: Christ put out the unbelieving crowds, and took with Him the girl's parents and a few of His disciples (Mk 5:40), that is, those who believe in His power. Then He took the girl by the hand and raised her, and her family and all the crowds rejoiced and glorified God who raises the dead.

9.18.1.en: And this is one of the many clear proofs of the divinity of Christ, who commanded death and it departed, and the girl arose, and the report spread in the lands surrounding Capernaum.

9.18.2.en: If you have faith, you will behold the great works of God. So do not be troubled if matters become complicated and it appears that there is no solution for them, for your God shows miracles in every generation and in ways that never cross your mind; only rely on Him, confident of His love and care.

9.19.s.en: (5) The healing of the two blind men

9.19.0.en: As Christ was walking along the road, two blind men followed Him, asking healing from Him. They represent the Jews and the Gentiles who fell into the darkness of sin and needed Christ the Savior to enlighten their lives. Christ let them cry out all along the way, to test their faith. And when He reached the house to which He was going, He asked them: Do you believe in my power to heal your eyes? So they declared their faith in Him as the awaited Messiah, the Son of David, who is able to open their eyes.

9.20.0.en: "According to your faith": God is rich and ready to give much, in proportion to what you believe of Him.

9.20.1.en: Then Christ touched their eyes, and commanded, and they regained their sight.

9.20.2.en: "Straitly charged them": that is, He forbade them to speak of the miracle, out of humility on His part, because He does not need the praise of men, in addition to His concern not to stir up the jealousy of the scribes and Pharisees, and lest they think of Him as an earthly king who would give them their material needs by freeing them from slavery to the Romans.

9.20.3.en: And He told them, in humility, not to tell anyone of this miracle.

9.20.4.en: Learn not to speak of your works in order to receive the praise of men, but do as Christ did, and God who sees you in secret will reward you openly.

9.21.0.en: When they saw the love and humility of Christ, they met His love with love also, so they went out proclaiming this miracle to everyone, since they wanted all to enjoy faith in Him, although it would have been better for them to obey Christ in not speaking of the miracle, because obedience is better than everything.

9.22.s.en: (6) The healing of the dumb and possessed man

9.22.0.en: Satan entered a man, and made him lose his mind, and prevented him from speaking. He represents the man subject to sin, whom Satan causes to lose his mind, and makes preoccupied with base lusts, and prevents him from speaking the word of God.

9.22.1.en: "They brought to him": this man needed people to lead him because he does not speak, in addition to having lost his mind. They brought this man to Christ, and He commanded Satan, by the authority of His divinity, to come out of him. And immediately he came out, and the man's mind returned and he spoke. So the crowds rejoiced and glorified God who had sent them a prophet who heals their diseases and saves them from the power of Satan.

9.22.2.en: "It was never so seen": that is, no prophet appeared in the history of the people of Israel who had this authority over demons and performed all these miracles.

9.23.0.en: But the Pharisees, the leaders of Jewish society, did not believe in the divinity of Christ or His authority over demons, but in their pride saw Him as a rival to them in leading the crowds, so they accused Him of having a relationship with "the prince of the devils," and that this is why He casts them out.

9.23.1.en: Pride makes you lose your understanding of matters, so that you do not see the works of God with you and in you. So be humble, and accept people's guidance for you, and seek God's direction every day, and submit to the word of your father of confession.

9.24.s.en: (7) Preaching in the cities and villages

9.24.0.en: Christ took care to visit the cities and also the villages, that is, the rich and the poor, and He did not center Himself in Capernaum or Jerusalem or only a large city, to show the importance of visitation. His preaching was the nearness of the Kingdom of Heaven and preparing for it by repentance. And He used to confirm His word with miracles, that people might believe His preaching.

9.25.0.en: The tender heart of Christ appears toward His children, whose leaders the Pharisees were too occupied to draw them to repentance, so He Himself took care to shepherd them.

9.25.1.en: "Troubled": this is the disturbance that accompanies falling into sin and being far from God. "Cast down": that is, exposed to the attacks of the devil and to falling into his sins.

9.26.0.en: The Lord directed the gaze of His disciples to the need of souls for someone to shepherd them, and likened them to stalks of wheat waiting for someone to reap their ears; but the reapers, that is, the leaders of Jewish society, were too occupied to serve because of their concern for their own dignity. And He did not tell the disciples to reap, but to ask God to send servants to shepherd His people, so that they might understand that it is God who calls servants to service, and not merely their own emotion or conviction about it; that is, they should pray, and God will move their feelings to care for souls, and then God sends them to His service. May you care for the salvation of the souls of those around you, so that you have compassion on all instead of being troubled by their many faults, and pray that God may move their hearts, for all are His children and created in His image, and He wants their salvation... And God either sends you to them, or sends them someone who brings them back to Him.

9.26.1.en: The calling of the disciples and their preaching in Judea
